brewing.notes: A safe starting point for yellow tea: treat it like a delicate green tea.

description:
A yellow tea from the Laoshan district of Qingdao in Shandong, on the Yellow Sea coast, made from one bud and one leaf.

Treat it as you would any yellow tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
name_ru: Лао Шань Юнь У Хуан Ча
history: Little is documented about it beyond its place among China's better known yellow tea areas.
processing: Young shoots are spread to cool, rolled, fixed, rolled again, lightly fermented and pan-fired.
harvest_season: Usually picked in early spring, as with most yellow teas.
taste_profile: A distinctive mellow aged aroma, a fresh and lively taste and a long sweet finish.
vintage_note: Yellow teas are normally sold as the current year's spring harvest and are best fresh.
